solution: By the Matrix–Tree Theorem, the number of spanning trees is the product of the nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues divided by 15. For the 3-by-5 grid, the eigenvalues are \(4-2\cos(\pi a/3)-2\cos(\pi b/5)\), where \(0\le a<3\), \(0\le b<5\). Omitting \((a,b)=(0,0)\), their product divided by 15 evaluates to 2415.
insight: The Laplacian eigenvalues of a rectangular grid are sums of the path-graph Laplacian eigenvalues for its two dimensions.
insight_justification: Each grid vertex has coordinates from two paths, and the grid Laplacian is the sum of the Laplacians acting along each coordinate. Thus eigenvectors formed from path eigenvectors have eigenvalues equal to the corresponding two path eigenvalues added.
